title: kobay plan file
description: A hand-written plan file, the input of `kobay test create --plan <path>`. One file is one test; a top-level array is not accepted. kobay turns the file into a draft test record and stops there — nothing is generated or run until `kobay test run <id>`. Give the test's page in `url` so failure analysis can compare the page against the exploration map; without it the analysis skips that comparison and says so in its output. Extra properties anywhere in the file are tolerated and ignored, so an editor directive such as `$schema` is safe to keep. This file mirrors the validator in `src/depo/semalar.ts`; where the two disagree, the validator is what actually runs.

projectId.description: Optional label for the project this test was written for. When present it must contain a non-whitespace character; kobay does not store it on the created test or match it against the current project, so any name you like works (older plan files that carry it keep working).

type.description: Must be the string `frontend`. kobay drives a browser, so this is the only test type it creates; any other value is rejected by name.

name.description: The test's name, kept as-is on the test record and shown by `test list` and `test get`. Must contain a non-whitespace character. Write it as the behavior you expect to hold, not as a noun fragment.

url.description: Optional. The page the test starts on: a path such as `/records`, or a full address on the project's `baseUrl` origin. It is kept on the test record; failure analysis and `kobay test refresh` use it to find the page in the exploration map. An address on another origin is rejected.

description.description: Optional free text explaining the test. Unlike `name`, any string passes, including an empty one. kobay does not copy it onto the test record; it is a note for whoever reads the plan file.

priority.description: Optional. How much this test matters: `p0` must pass, `p1` covers the paths you care about, `p2` edge cases, `p3` cosmetic. Left out, the test is created as `p1`.

planSteps.description: Between 1 and 200 steps, in the order the test should walk them. Write intent in plain language — the step text is what the brain reads when it generates the Playwright code, so a step that names a CSS selector teaches it nothing. The text is taken literally — kobay fills in no placeholders and reads no variables — and it is kept verbatim on the test record.

type.description: `action` does something to the app (open a page, fill a field, click). `assertion` checks something is true. A test whose steps are all actions checks nothing.

description.description: What this one step does or checks. Must contain a non-whitespace character. One step, one verb.
examples: At least one record row is visible

planSteps.description: At least one record row is visible
